q: Does CO2 used as welding shielding gas count in Scope 1?
title: CO2 welding gas in Scope 1
short: Yes. CO2 released at your site from cylinders or bulk tanks is a direct emission, so it is Scope 1 at its mass, usually small next to fuel and power. For mixed gases count only the CO2 share. Argon is not a greenhouse gas. Welder electricity is Scope 2.

ol: Add up kg of CO2 bought from cylinder or bulk invoices.
Adjust for stock at the start and end of the year.
For mixtures, multiply by the CO2 percentage on the label.

ul: If it is small, you can say so and include it anyway; leaving it out needs a stated reason.
Making the gas is the supplier's emission, reported in your Scope 3 if you choose to include it.
